research_question: What is the effect of digital health, technology-driven or technology-assisted interventions combined with conventional care, compared with conventional care alone, on waist circumference (cm) at the end of the study in children and adolescents (aged 0 to 19 years) with overweight or obesity?
treatment_label: Digital health or technology-assisted intervention combined with conventional care
outcome_description: Waist circumference in centimeters (cm) measured at the end of the intervention or study period
positive_direction: A positive effect indicates a larger waist circumference in the digital health plus conventional care group compared with conventional care alone (i.e., higher waist circumference)
search_queries: digital health pediatric obesity waist circumference randomized trial
technology assisted intervention children overweight conventional care controlled trial
mHealth mobile app adolescent obesity waist circumference trial
inclusion_criteria: Children and adolescents (aged 0 to 19 years) diagnosed with overweight or obesity
Evaluation of a digital health, technology-driven, or technology-assisted intervention combined with conventional care compared to conventional care alone
Reporting of quantitative endpoint data for waist circumference
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, commentaries, opinion pieces, conference abstracts without full data, and theoretical papers are excluded)
No comparison between a digital health/technology-assisted intervention plus conventional care and conventional care alone
No quantitative outcome data that can produce an effect size for waist circumference (e.g., means and SDs, change scores, or exact test statistics)
Completely unrelated to pediatric overweight/obesity or digital health/technology interventions
moderators_to_extract: Mean participant age or age category (children vs. adolescents)
Type of digital health technology (e.g., smartphone application, SMS text messaging, wearable tracker, web-based platform)
Involvement of parents/caregivers (parent-targeted vs. child-only vs. dual)
